title: Conversational Re-entrancy Architecture Clinic — Notes and Decisions
content:
Meeting: Conversational Re-entrancy Architecture Clinic
Date: 2025-06-02
Attendees: Leah O'Connor (facilitator), Ravi Patel, Maya Chen, Oliver Grant, Priya Nair, Samir Desai
Slack thread: #arch-clinic-reentrancy (see pinned snippets)
Purpose: Triage RFC concerns about guaranteeing safe retries, partial-stream replay, and consistent KV-cache state for multi-turn conversations. We need a pragmatic design that fits hosted + dedicated + private deployments.

Summary / problem statement:
- Observed failure mode: downstream client retries or network re-ordering can cause the runtime to replay partial inputs leading to duplicated tokens or state divergence (e.g., repeated system prompts, duplicate assistant turns).
- Requirements: preserve low-latency for normal requests, provide strong-enough idempotency for typical app patterns (retry-on-timeout, streaming reconnects), keep storage overhead modest, and work within Private deployment constraints (no cross-tenant global sequencer).
- Non-goals: full distributed transaction semantics, guaranteeing cross-model multi-stage ACID. We want practical, operationally maintainable guarantees.

Important constraints called out:
- Many customers use streaming + chunked uploads and will re-open streams (partial replay).
- Private deployments cannot rely on a global central sequencer or hosted control-plane for per-request coordination.
- Maintaining per-session metadata in hotstore impacts memory pressure; retention window must be bounded.

Options discussed (high-level):
1) Global sequencer (centralized monotonic sequence numbers per session)
   - How it works: each incoming top-level request obtains a monotonically increasing sequence token (centralized service). Requests carrying older tokens are rejected/ignored in the runtime or used with dedupe logic.
   - Pros: clear ordering, simple detection of duplicates/replays.
   - Cons: single point of coordination, cross-tenant/global service not allowed for Private; introduces extra RTT (bad for low-latency hosted routes) and requires highly-available control plane.

2) Per-session idempotency tokens + best-effort dedupe in runtime (optimistic, local-only) — RECOMMENDED BASELINE
   - How it works: clients attach an idempotency token per logical user action (e.g., request attempt). The runtime stores recent token -> last-ack mapping in session metadata (hotstore with bounded TTL). On replays, runtime dedupes by token and resumes/returns previous response or safely resumes. For stream reconnects, the client includes last acknowledged chunk index + token.
   - Enhancements: allow optional per-tenant sequencer for Dedicated/Hosted enterprise customers that opt-in for stronger ordering; use short retention window (e.g., 5m–30m) configurable per deployment class.
   - Pros: simple to implement in runtime, works offline for Private, minimal extra control-plane dependencies, low added latency for most requests.
   - Cons: best-effort semantics — token loss or TTL expiry leads to replay; requires client adoption (library + SDK changes).

3) Shadow-versions + CRDT-ish merge for conversation state (stateless replay + idempotent apply)
   - How it works: requests include an action-id; runtime persists ephemeral shadow writes per action; model state updates are applied with versioned cursors enabling safe replay/merge.
   - Pros: strong convergence guarantees, good for multi-writer sessions in theory.
   - Cons: complex, storage-heavy, requires model and prompt-side adaptations, longer delivery timeline, incompatible with many existing customer setups.

Discussion notes and tradeoffs:
- We considered a pure client-side approach (clients responsible for dedupe) but agreed runtime assistance improves developer experience and reduces bug surface.
- For streaming reconnects, the critical helper pieces are: (a) last acked token/index, (b) consistent resume semantics in the runtime's stream framing, and (c) light-weight token dedupe table in session metadata.
- Privacy/regulatory concern: tokens are per-request non-sensitive identifiers; we must publish guidance to avoid embedding PII. For Private, retention defaults can be zero with explicit opt-in for retention windows.
- KV cache interactions: when deduping, runtime must avoid double-applying prefix prefetches; dedupe table should be consulted before modifying cache hot entries. We added a small flow chart to the RFC draft (see Confluence link).

Decision (consensus): Adopt Option 2 as the baseline approach for the next milestone with the following augmentations:
- Runtime will implement a per-session recent-idempotency-table stored in session hotstore with pluggable retention policy. Default retention: 300s for hosted, 120s for dedicated, 0s for private (configurable).
- SDKs will be updated to emit idempotency_token and last_ack_index for streaming flows. Backward compatibility: if token missing, runtime falls back to best-effort heuristics (timestamp dedupe within 30s bucket).
- Provide an opt-in per-tenant sequencer module for customers who require strict ordering (Dedicated + Hosted enterprise). This will be deployed as an optional service in the Dedicated control plane and requires an explicit flag in tenant config.
- Add a runtime pre-check hook: when an idempotency token is seen, consult the dedupe table and, if duplicate, return stored result or a small resume envelope rather than re-running the full model path.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How to surface dedupe hits to observability? Proposed metric: runtime.dedupe.hits and runtime.dedupe.misses, and a histogram of dedupe latency. Action: Maya to draft observability spec.
- TTL sizing tradeoffs vs memory pressure. Need simulated workload to validate. Action: Ravi to run a stress job (INF-2207) modeling conversation churn and return numbers by 2025-06-16.
- Failure modes when hotstore replica lag occurs. If dedupe table read is stale, we may re-run requests. Need to classify acceptable risk. Action: Samir to produce a short doc mapping consistency modes to customer SLO impact by 2025-06-13.
- Privacy default for Private deployments: retention default 0s. Need explicit admin API to opt-in and store audit log. Priya to add to Private deployment checklist (JIRA INF-2201).

Operational runbook items required before canary:
- Migration plan: SDK release -> runtime flag -> canary on low-traffic tenants. Document rollback steps and a quick inspector to enumerate recently seen idempotency tokens for a session.
- Canary success criteria: <0.1% increase in average latency on canary tenants, dedupe hits visible with expected rate, no spike in cache thrash.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Implement runtime idempotency table prototype (Leah + Oliver) — prototype branch by 2025-06-09 (PR: runtime/poc/reentrancy).
- SDK change: add idempotency token + last_ack_index fields (Maya) — draft SDK PR by 2025-06-11.
- Observability spec: metrics + dashboards (Maya) — draft by 2025-06-10.
- Workload sim and memory-pressure study (Ravi) — sim results + recommendation by 2025-06-16 (JIRA INF-2207).
- Private deployment policy (Priya) — admin opt-in + audit log design by 2025-06-12 (JIRA INF-2201).
- Consistency failure modes doc (Samir) — by 2025-06-13.

Follow-ups / next meetings:
- Implementation sync: 2025-06-06 10:00 PT (sync on prototype progress).
- Canaries review: 2025-06-18 (initial canary results + decision to expand).

Notes to implementation team:
- Keep implementation small and feature-flagged. Start with an in-memory hotstore-backed table (existing session hotstore abstraction); ensure TTL enforcement is off the hot path where possible (lazy cleanup).
- Provide a small API for stored-result retrieval; stored-result should be a compact resume envelope (status, last_chunk_index, final_output_reference) rather than storing full generated tokens to save memory.
- Document SDK expectations: token generation recommended pattern (uuidv4 + optional client prefix) and guidance to avoid embedding PII.

Appendix / links referenced in discussion:
- RFC draft: Conversation Re-entrancy — runtime proposal (internal) (Confluence link above).
- Related JIRAs: INF-2201 (Private policy), INF-2207 (capacity sim for dedupe table).
- Example SDK snippet (will be added to SDK PR):
  const token = client.genIdempotencyToken();
  await client.streamChat({ prompt, idempotency_token: token, last_ack_index });

End of notes.

Quick decisions snapshot (for inbox):
- Baseline: per-session idempotency tokens + runtime dedupe table (Option 2) — agreed.
- Opt-in: per-tenant sequencer for Dedicated/Hosted enterprise customers.
- Private default: 0s retention unless explicitly enabled.

Recorded by: Leah O'Connor
Status: draft — please add comments inline on Confluence or file follow-up issues against the linked JIRAs.
